title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Ribera and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show Ribera del Duero DO, the producer, vintage and ageing category, with a back-label seal. Roble, oak, is an unofficial term for young wines with a few months in barrel. Many top wines don't use the categories at all, relying on the producer's name.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Ribera's classic pairing is lechazo, roast suckling lamb, cooked in wood-fired clay ovens in Aranda de Duero. It also suits grilled steak, game, chorizo, Manchego and aged sheep's cheese. Serve at 16 to 18 degrees, decanted when young; good Ribera ages 10 to 20 years.

steps.prompt: Which dish is Ribera del Duero's classic match?
steps.explanation: Roast suckling lamb in wood ovens.

steps.body: Aranda de Duero has a network of medieval underground cellars, many still used for ageing wine.

steps.prompt: Roble is an official Spanish ageing category.
steps.explanation: Not true. It's an informal term for young wines with brief oak ageing.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show the category; Roble is informal
Ribera's classic match is roast suckling lamb
Serve decanted; good wines age 10 to 20 years
